- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.5) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted overshoot by 10–20% in the immediate aftermath.
- Mean-reversion bias is common in 30-day forecasts; adjust downward if recent 7–14 day average is significantly above 30-day average.
- If sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days after forecast, reduce forecast by 5–15% to account for reversal risk.
- Forecast should not exceed 2 standard deviations above recent 18-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish and confirmed by multiple indicators.
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome is below forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 3–7% to avoid further overcorrection.
